question.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}uv \\ u+v\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-{u}^{2} \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the cross term $uv.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ -u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{1}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term ${u}^{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ only."
